question: In a few countries, inland navigation fuel is now blended with biological components, under the Fuel Quality Directive (FQD) and the Renewable Energy Directive (RED III). The switch should not, in theory, cause problems for engines. However, concerns persist among some in the sector.

The Algemeene Schippers Vereeniging ASV, a Dutch inland shipping association, advised its members in May to bunker only unblended diesel. The organisation warned ‘that widely used biofuels, in particular FAME (Fatty Acid Methyl Ester), are causing technical problems’1. A boatmaster told me that he suspects that fuel containing animal fats damages engines, in particular the fuel pump and injectors.
Others, however, consider these concerns to be unjustified. 1.
Does the Commission have any information indicating that fuel which fully complies with EN 590 and EN 14214 causes structural damage to engines under normal conditions of use?
Is the Commission prepared to standardise fuel and blending (HVO/FAME) for inland shipping in the same way as for road transport?
